claim: On a standard Borel probability sample space, any Nat-indexed family of adapted measurable [0,1] tests with strictly positive summable registered budgets alpha_j and sum alpha_j<=delta<=1 has one event of probability at least 1-delta on which every positive-time observed residual minus its actual conditional-expectation drift obeys sqrt(t/2*log(2t(t+1)/alpha_j)). The event supports arbitrary selected times/rules and nonnegative scalar multiplication of an already-bounded residual.

validation.scope: Fresh supported-source acceptance only. Author isolated replay and parent release verification are separate evidence.

assumptions: StandardBorelSpace Omega for the ambient sample measurable space; actual probability measure mu.
Filtration F_i is increasing and below the ambient sigma algebra. Every X_{j,i} is measurable at F_{i+1}, and is in [0,1] mu-almost surely.
Rules are indexed by all natural numbers; alpha_j are strictly positive NNReal, summable, and sum_j alpha_j<=delta<=1.
The drift uses actual mu[X_{j,i}|F_i], not a supplied mean or MGF hypothesis. Model predictions p cancel algebraically; predictable p is a valid intended specialization.
Selected time is encoded as time(omega)+1, covering every positive selected time; selected rule may also depend on data.
dependency_graph: A conditioning-measurable function g is conditionally constant: push the diagonal joint law through compProd_trim_condExpKernel, then disintegrate the measurable equality set g(second)=g(first).
A bounded test has integrable actual conditional expectation in [0,1]. Global centered residual lies in [-1,1], which supplies exponential integrability.

Under almost every conditional kernel, X remains in [0,1], the conditional mean is the kernel integral, and that mean is constant along the kernel fiber. Apply ordinary Hoeffding to X under the kernel, then transfer to X-E[X|F]. This yields conditional MGF proxy1/4.
The partial centered sum S_n is F_n-measurable. Trim its unconditional MGF to F_n and use conditional-MGF addition with the next increment; induction gives proxy n/4 without independence.
Two-sided Chernoff tails at b>=0 give probability <=2 exp(-2b^2/n) for every n>0.
At the displayed boundary, this tail is alpha/[n(n+1)]. Finite telescoping proves summability and total time budget<=alpha.
Countable union over time yields one-rule all-time coverage. A second countable union over registered rules spends total<=delta.
Observed residual minus actual drift cancels model predictions pointwise and equals the centered sum, giving the simultaneous certificate.
The pathwise all-time/all-rule event specializes to any selected positive time and rule; multiplying that existing inequality by c>=0 scales its boundary.

obligation_matrix.obligation: The conditional mean is constructed using actual conditional expectation, rather than assumed centeredness.
The1/4 proxy comes from conditional width-one X, not the wider global centered residual interval[-1,1].
Kernel centering uses a measurable fiber-constancy statement and the actual conditional-integral representation.
Induction preserves adaptedness and applies a conditional-MGF theorem rather than an independence theorem.
Time indexing aligns X_i with information F_i before observation and F_{i+1} afterward; range n sums i=0..n-1.
Boundary logarithm and square-root simplification retain n>0 and0<alpha<=1.
Time weights are1/[(n+1)(n+2)], matching the positive-time n(n+1) tail budget.
All bad events are measurable; strict boundary violations are bounded by the non-strict Chernoff events.
The final confidence event is simultaneous over all positive times and Nat-indexed rules with one delta budget.
No measurability of arbitrary model p is needed for the displayed residual-minus-drift event because p cancels exactly.
Selected times/rules need no new confidence spending; scalar scaling is a valid separate pathwise implication.
